title: When light traveled freely
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: Before neutral atoms formed, free electrons frequently scattered photons. Once many electrons combined with nuclei, photons traveled much more freely through the universe.

misconception: A learner may choose: All photons were destroyed
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: Why did the early universe become much more transparent after neutral atoms formed?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: Why did the early universe become much more transparent after neutral atoms formed? Photons scattered less often from free electrons. Before neutral atoms formed, free electrons frequently scattered photons. Once many electrons combined with nuclei, photons traveled much more freely through the universe.
Visual caption: Fewer free electrons. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.
